title: Probability and statistics for computing
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn probability and statistics as computer scientists use them: probability spaces, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' rule, random variables, expectation, linearity and indicators, variance and common distributions, the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem, tail bounds, Markov chains, estimation and confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests and A/B tests, with simulation.
primary_reading: Introduction to Probability by Blitzstein and Hwang (free online, Harvard Stat 110)

weeks.7: Continuous distributions and the normal distribution
weeks.8: The law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
weeks.9: Tail bounds: Markov, Chebyshev and Chernoff

blocks.deliverable: Solve ten probability problems and check them by simulation.
Apply Bayes' rule to a spam-filter example.
Compute expected costs of randomized algorithms.
Week 7 midterm; simulate the central limit theorem.
Bound the failure probability of a randomized algorithm.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Simulation and analysis study: write Python simulations for three supplied problems (for example a hash-collision question, the cost of randomized quicksort and a waiting line), compare them with exact calculations, and analyze a supplied A/B-test data set in a written report.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L07.txt: Continuous distributions and the normal distribution
files.L08.txt: The law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
